evidence.text: South India, Tamil Nadu, Chola period (900–1200s)

placements.note: The record names present-day Tamil Nadu and the Chola period but no place of production, so the work is shown as a regional association.

evidence.text: Northern India, Uttar Pradesh, Mathura, Kushan period

placements.note: The museum attributes the work to Mathura, a major centre of Kushan-period sculpture. The record does not state where it was made or found.

evidence.text: Northeastern India, Bihar, Tetravan, Pala Period (750-1197)

placements.note: The record also names Tetravan, a village in Bihar. Its location could not be verified from a reliable source, so the work is shown at the state level rather than pinned to a guessed village.
Only the present-day state is recorded; no site, city or period is given.

evidence.text: It was carved by one of the finest craftsmen in the Eastern Wei capital of Ye in Hebei province.

placements.note: The museum's description places the carving in Ye, the Eastern Wei capital. The marker shows the ancient city, not a specific workshop.

evidence.text: China, Hebei province, Southern Xiangtangshan caves, Northern Qi dynasty (550-577)

placements.note: The museum attributes the figure to the Southern Xiangtangshan cave temples (and exhibited it in “Echoes of the Past: The Buddhist Cave Temples at Xiangtangshan”). The record does not identify the cave.

evidence.text: China, probably Henan province, Tang dynasty (618–907)

placements.note: The museum gives Henan as probable, not certain, and records no site.

evidence.text: China, reportedly from Hunan province, Changsha, Warring States period (475–221 BCE), State of Chu (c. 1046–223 BCE)

placements.note: The find site is reported, not confirmed: the museum says “reportedly from … Changsha”, and a 1930s study cited in the record describes the work as “said to have been discovered in Chang-sha”.
